result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Whole-application inspection of SecurityConfig, all controllers/services/models, both production property profiles, Dockerfile, Compose, Oracle startup/verification scripts and .env.example; credentials inspected with values redacted.

Runtime passwords are required environment inputs (application.properties:14; application-docker.properties:5; SecurityConfig.java:35; docker-compose.yml:7,10,36,38). .env.example:6,12,17 are explicitly documented replace-before-use placeholders, not confirmed production credentials. BCrypt uses framework-generated salt; no hard-coded crypto key found. Public gallery access is explicit design, and Oracle startup grants are schema-scoped rather than DBA.
limitations: No environment secrets, live deployment permissions, ingress configuration, authentication attempts or emitted runtime logs inspected. External audit/monitoring could mitigate the source-level logging gap. Placeholder examples and test-only credentials were not classified as production secrets. NOT_FOUND indicates no confirmed application instance, not proof of absence.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: Authentication audit gap: SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain (44-58) enables default HTTP Basic authentication on upload/delete without an authentication-failure audit handler or application authentication-event listener; no such listener exists elsewhere in the whole application. Neither property profile enables Spring Security authentication DEBUG logging or HTTP access logging. Failed credential attempts therefore have no configured durable security audit record, limiting brute-force investigation. Application delete logging (DetailController.deletePhoto, 64-75) records photo ID but no authenticated actor or request source. Framework authentication events alone are not persisted audit records; external ingress/audit logging is not present in the repository.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
